name: Gabapentin
sections: White to off-white crystalline solid, freely soluble in water.

Initially approved as add-on therapy for refractory epilepsy; later approved for post-herpetic neuralgia (2002). Generics available since 2004. First approval/introduction: Synthesised 1974–75 (Goedecke AG / Parke-Davis); UK May 1993; US FDA December 1993.

Binds the alpha-2-delta subunit of voltage-gated calcium channels in the CNS, reducing calcium influx and release of excitatory neurotransmitters (glutamate, substance P, norepinephrine). Receptor / target profile: Binds alpha-2-delta subunits of voltage-gated calcium channels, modulating calcium influx and excitatory neurotransmitter release; despite being a GABA analogue it does not act on GABA receptors.
27–60% (inversely proportional to dose; saturable L-amino acid transport)

Summary: Saturable absorption – bioavailability falls with dose (60% at 900 mg/day to 27% at 4800 mg/day). Tmax 2–3 h. <3% protein bound; not metabolised. Half-life 5–7 h. Renally excreted – adjust to CrCl.
Peripheral neuropathic pain (diabetic neuropathy, post-herpetic neuralgia)
Partial seizures with or without secondary generalisation (adjunct or monotherapy)
Neuropathic pain: day 1 – 300 mg; day 2 – 600 mg; day 3 – 900 mg (divided three times daily); titrate to 1800–3600 mg/day
Low starting doses (100 mg three times daily) for elderly/frail patients
Epilepsy: 900–3600 mg/day in three divided doses (max interval 12 h)
Renal impairment: dose according to CrCl
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
CrCl 30–59: 400–1400 mg/day; 15–29: 200–700 mg/day; <15: 100–300 mg/day; supplemental dose after haemodialysis.
Adjust to renal function; dizziness, falls.
Use only if benefit outweighs risk.
Respiratory depression, particularly with opioids, CNS depressants, elderly or respiratory disease
Reduce dose in renal impairment; taper over ≥1 week
Opioids (morphine raises gabapentin levels; respiratory depression)
Antacids with Al/Mg reduce absorption ~20% – take gabapentin ≥2 h later
With or without food; separate Al/Mg antacids by ≥2 hours; avoid alcohol.
Renal function; mood; respiratory status with opioids; misuse.
Dizziness, double vision, slurred speech, drowsiness, lethargy, diarrhoea. Supportive care; haemodialysis effective.
Cochrane review (Wiffen et al., 2017) – gabapentin 1200 mg/day or more: NNT ~6–8 for substantial pain relief in post-herpetic neuralgia and diabetic neuropathy.
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
